text: Appendix II provides the mapping of the architectural components and supporting architectural aspects to the high-level requirements provided in clause 7. 8.2 High-level architecture The high-level architecture shown in Figure 4 is derived from the high-level requirements specified in clause 7 and builds upon the architectural components described in clause 8.1. Rec. ITU-T Y.3172 (06/2019) 17 Figure 4 - High-level architecture The reference points shown in Figure 4 are the following: 1, 2: These are the data handling reference points between simulated ML underlay networks and an ML pipeline in an ML sandbox subsystem. 3: This is the reference point between an ML sandbox subsystem and an ML pipeline subsystem. 4: This is the reference point between an ML pipeline subsystem and ML underlay networks. NOTE 1 - This reference point represents the data handling reference points shown as arrows 3 and 4 in Figure 3. 5, 6: These are the reference points between the management subsystem and, the ML pipeline subsystem and ML sandbox subsystem, respectively. 7: This is the reference point between the MLFO and other management and orchestration functions of the management subsystem. 8, 9: These are the reference points between ML pipeline nodes located in different levels. The three subsystems of the high-level architecture as shown in Figure 4 are given below. • Management subsystem This subsystem includes the MLFO and other management and orchestration functions, e.g., those defined in [ITU-T Y.3111]. The management subsystem enables the extension of the management and orchestration mechanisms used for future networks including IMT-2020 to ML pipeline nodes. This brings uniformity to the management of ML functionalities and NFs. 18 Rec. ITU-T Y.3172 (06/2019) The MLFO works in coordination with the other functions of the management subsystem to manage the ML pipeline nodes. NOTE 2 - The reference point(s) between the functions of the management subsystem and NFs in the ML underlay networks complies(y) with the reference points defined in the related specifications, e.g., [ITU-T Y.3111]. These reference points are out of scope of this Recommendation and thus are not shown in Figure 4. NOTE 3 - The interaction between the MLFO and the other functions of the management subsystem may be achieved using service-based architecture (SBA). • ML pipeline subsystem The ML pipeline is a logical pipeline that can be overlaid on existing network infrastructures. The services of the MLFO are used for instantiation and set-up. Integration aspects of such ML pipeline overlay on technology-specific ML underlay networks may require the extension or definition of specific protocols and APIs. In addition, the following points are to be noted: - SBA may be used for interfacing between NFs and ML pipeline nodes as well as between ML pipeline nodes themselves.

text: Integration aspects of such ML pipeline overlay on technology-specific ML underlay networks may require the extension or definition of specific protocols and APIs. In addition, the following points are to be noted: - SBA may be used for interfacing between NFs and ML pipeline nodes as well as between ML pipeline nodes themselves. As a first example, an SRC node exposes interfaces for consuming data from the NFs and producing data towards the collector (C) node. As a second example, a SINK node exposes interfaces for consuming the ML output from the distributor (D) node and produces such configurations to the NFs which it interfaces with. NOTE 4 - Due to the heterogeneity of NFs and ML underlay networks, SBA may not be supported by NFs in the ML underlay networks. In such cases, protocols and APIs specific to those ML underlay networks are used between the ML pipeline nodes and the NFs. - The placement and chaining of the ML pipeline nodes are controlled by the MLFO and this control may be influenced by factors such as: • inputs from the ML Intent to the MLFO which may impose constraints on the placement of ML pipeline nodes. NOTE 5 - The requirement to place an ML model (M) node on a network computing resource which provides a specific type of acceleration capability is an example of constraints on the placement of an M node. • Feedback received by the MLFO from the management and orchestration functions of the ML underlay networks or from the ML pipeline nodes may provide inputs on the placement and chaining of ML pipeline nodes. NOTE 6 - Decoupling of the location of the ML pipeline nodes from their functionalities, except in the case of performance constraints, is achieved using the placement and chaining mechanisms. - The deployment of an ML pipeline in future networks including IMT-2020 may span different levels. In this case, reference points between nodes located in different levels of an ML pipeline are used to allow ML pipeline multilevel distribution. NOTE 7 - As shown in Figure 4, an ML pipeline may be distributed over multiple levels, e.g., a specific deployment may distribute the pipeline across a UE, AN and CN. Based on the specific ML application, different ways of distributing the ML pipeline nodes are possible. • ML sandbox subsystem An ML sandbox subsystem allows ML pipelines to adapt to dynamic network environments such as those of future networks including IMT-2020 where a variety of conditions may change (e.g., air interface conditions, UE position, network capabilities and resources).

title: T-REC-Y.3172-201906-I!!PDF-E

text: Based on the specific ML application, different ways of distributing the ML pipeline nodes are possible. • ML sandbox subsystem An ML sandbox subsystem allows ML pipelines to adapt to dynamic network environments such as those of future networks including IMT-2020 where a variety of conditions may change (e.g., air interface conditions, UE position, network capabilities and resources). The ML sandbox subsystem includes ML pipeline(s) and simulated ML underlay networks, and it is managed by the MLFO according to the specifications in the ML Intent. The ML sandbox subsystem allows network operators to study the effect of ML outputs before deploying them on live ML underlay networks. Feedback from the functions of the management subsystem is provided to the ML sandbox subsystem Rec. ITU-T Y.3172 (06/2019) 19 so that the ML pipelines of the ML sandbox subsystem can adapt to the dynamically changing network environments. The following points are to be noted: - The reference point between the ML pipeline subsystem and ML sandbox subsystem allows the ML pipelines to interface with the ML sandbox subsystem for the training and updating of ML models. - Data from the ML underlay networks and/or the simulated ML underlay networks may be used to train the ML models in the ML sandbox subsystem. - The management of the ML pipeline nodes in the ML sandbox subsystem is also controlled by the MLFO. This allows the MLFO to train and select the ML model(s) for a given ML application. 8.3 General guidelines for realization of the high-level architecture General guidelines for realization of the high-level architecture on different technology-specific underlay networks are as follows: • Instantiation of the ML pipeline nodes: An ML application is described using ML Intent. The flow of information in an ML application can be represented by the chaining in an ML pipeline. The data from various source nodes, e.g., coming from various underlying networks, need to be gathered (by a collector node) and preprocessed (by a preprocessor node) before feeding this data to the ML model (model node). The output of the ML model is then used to apply policies (by a policy node) that will be implemented (by a SINK node). An ML application can be realized by instantiating nodes of the ML pipeline with specific roles (e.g., SRC, C, SINK), and associating these nodes to the technology-specific underlying network functions, based on the corresponding requirements of the ML application and the capabilities of the underlying network functions. The instantiation is performed by the MLFO in coordination with the other management and orchestration functions. • Interfacing of ML application with underlying network functions:

text: The instantiation is performed by the MLFO in coordination with the other management and orchestration functions. • Interfacing of ML application with underlying network functions: There are two points of specific interfacing with the underlying network functions for an ML application, the SRC and the SINK nodes. The SRC nodes may have either an SBA based interface to the associated NFs which produce data or a technology-specific interface for non-SBA capable NFs. Similarly, the SINK nodes may have an SBA based interface to the associated NFs which enforce the ML output policies or a technology-specific interface for non-SBA capable NFs. • Management of the ML pipeline: This is done by the MLFO in coordination with the other management and orchestration functions. • ML model training and evaluation in the ML sandbox: This is controlled by the MLFO independently of the ML underlay networks. The reference point between the ML sandbox subsystem and ML pipeline subsystem is used to transfer trained ML models, data for training and ML model updates between the ML sandbox subsystem and the ML underlay networks which interact with the live ML pipeline.

Table II.1 - Mapping of the architectural components and supporting aspects to the requirements Architectural components and supporting aspects Requirements Mapping explanation ML pipeline See clauses 7.1 and 7.2. The ML pipeline provides a common vocabulary for ML in future networks including IMT-2020. By defining the ML pipeline nodes, it becomes possible to consider the evolution of ML separately from the underlay networks. Instantiation of these nodes form an important part of deployment of ML overlay on different underlay networks. The functions of these nodes are defined independently of their location in the network, and hence this allows flexible placement of such nodes in the network. Split, merge and chaining of ML pipeline nodes allows deploying complex functions from these basic nodes. MLFO See clauses 7.2, 7.4 and 7.5 The MLFO orchestrates and manages the ML pipeline nodes. It is also responsible for optimal placement and chaining of ML pipeline nodes in the network. It implements these functions in coordination with the management and orchestration functions. The declarative specifications of the ML applications are supported by the MLFO by converting them into underlay-specific deployments. It also selects the models and reselects them based on the needs of the ML applications and other constraints defined in the ML Intent. ML sandbox See clause 7.5 This subsystem provides the ability to train, evaluate and monitor the performance of ML models before deploying them in a real network. It interfaces with the underlay networks for the transfer of data or trained models. In addition, it uses the simulated ML underlay networks which may generate data required for training the ML models. 24 Rec. title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 1: Data/Model Marketplace (data_marketplace)

Measures the creation of an ecosystem for startups, B2B, or other value-providers to create services from (un)structured data, expert knowledge base, and general platform, and monetize them.

Mapped Factors: data, opensource

Metrics:
- d1_m01 Dataset Properties: Properties of datasets (metadata: types structured/unstructured, number of datasets, volume, velocity, variety, quality)
- d1_m02 Model Properties: Properties of models (metadata: types, size, performance, ML/DL, i/o, training dataset parameters)
- d1_m03 Data Collection Sources: Location, heterogeneity, number of sources, privacy/trust, synthetic/real world, type of source
- d1_m04 Diligence Metrics: License and participation agreement templates for marketplace trust
- d1_m05 Marketplace Activity: Number of data producers, consumers, agreements, transactions in the data marketplace
- d1_m06 Open Datasets: Number of open datasets, downloads, global citations
- d1_m07 Marketplace Participants: Number of active participants and transaction frequencies
- d1_m08 Fairness and Bias: Safeguards to manage data bias or data quality risks
- d1_m09 Privacy and Security: Privacy-preserving mechanisms, authentication, authorization, just-in-time deletion
- d1_m10 Personal Data Standards: Standards on personal data protection
- d1_m11 Data Governance: Percentage of datasets under partner agreements, license metrics
- d1_m12 Standards-Compliant Formats: Amount of data available in pre-specified standard and interoperable manner
- d1_m13 Open-Source Models: Properties of open-source models, openly published weights, number of open-source models by domain

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 2: Generated Content Marketplace (generated_content)

Measures the ease of creation of new services using AI, including new datasets/models generated for new AI services.

Mapped Factors: data, opensource

Metrics:
- d2_m01 Ecosystem Parameters: Datasets, models for content generation, pluggability, trading/monetization
- d2_m02 Guardrails: Availability of guardrails for hallucinations and ethical content
- d2_m03 Multi-modal Support: Support for multi-modal content generation
- d2_m04 Fake Detection: Evaluation techniques for fake detection
- d2_m05 Regional Customization: Customization mechanisms for regional content

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 3: Cross-Domain Correlation Analysis (cross_domain)

Measures cross-domain correlation in integrating AI, finding similarities and patterns in different domain workflows and opportunities for AI integration.

Mapped Factors: data, standards

Metrics:
- d3_m01 Integrated Workflow: Existence of integrated workflow including prevention, detection, response, and impact analysis
- d3_m02 Domain Status: Status of application domains using available data and regional readiness parameters
- d3_m03 Domain Models: Domain-specific workflows/models
- d3_m04 Domain KPIs: Domain-specific KPIs
- d3_m05 Infrastructure Representation: Availability of representation schemes for infrastructure deployment
- d3_m06 Cycle Time Reduction: Benefits due to correlation: cycle time reduction via integrated workflows
- d3_m07 Coverage and Scale: Coverage in terms of area and scale in terms of deployments

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 4: Contextualization and Regional Impact (contextualization)

Handles indigenous solutions, contextualization with regional inputs for maximizing community impact, and adoption level of regional solutions at larger scale.

Mapped Factors: data, research, deployment

Metrics:
- d4_m01 Regional Innovation: Number/quality of regionally developed patents, technology components, solutions
- d4_m02 Local Datasets: Availability of structured and accessible local datasets for training AI models
- d4_m03 Indigenous Service Users: Number of users of indigenous services
- d4_m04 Regional Customizations: Generalized vs. contextualized solutions with local inputs
- d4_m05 Technology Adoption: Adoption and scaling of local technologies in other markets
- d4_m06 Knowledge Products: Number of localized standard operating procedures, after-action reviews, hybrid AI playbooks
- d4_m07 Cultural Diversity: Cultural diversity brought by regional inputs
- d4_m08 Best Practices Adoption: Number of new regions adopting AI-based workflow from other regions
- d4_m09 Sub-group Representation: Representation of sub-groups in dataset for fine-tuning, prompt-tuning or evaluations

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 5: Level of Integration of AI in Workflows (ai_integration)

Measures how well AI is integrated into domain workflows and how many benefits it provides. AI is seen as a tool to optimize different domain workflows.

Mapped Factors: standards

Metrics:
- d5_m01 Automation Level: Level of automation achieved by integrating AI
- d5_m02 Benefits: Benefits achieved by integrating AI
- d5_m03 Time/Energy Saved: Time and energy saved through AI integration
- d5_m04 Efficiency: Efficiency metrics including containment time
- d5_m05 Redundancy: Redundancy in AI-integrated systems
- d5_m06 Scalability: Scalability of AI techniques
- d5_m07 Integration Level: Level of AI integration at design, coding, and evaluation levels
- d5_m08 Model Suitability: Discovery and suitability of model and dataset for the workflow
- d5_m09 Service Multiplier: Number of AI services for the same set of resources
- d5_m10 Quality Improvement: Improvement in quality of services by integrating AI
- d5_m11 Scope Extension: Extension of scope and range of services
- d5_m12 Cost Reduction: Demonstrable reduction in cost for similar services

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 6: Human Interface (human_interface)

Measures the use of AI for ease of human interaction with systems/workflows across various devices.

Mapped Factors: standards, deployment

Metrics:
- d6_m01 AI-Ready Interface Penetration: Availability/penetration of applications with AI-ready human interface
- d6_m02 Local Language Models: Availability of AI models in the local language used in the human interface
- d6_m03 Interaction Channels: Channels and devices (mobiles, kiosks, smart panels, sensors, wearables) for human-AI interaction
- d6_m04 Usability Level: Usability level of AI-integrated applications and services
- d6_m05 Cultural Sensitivity: Level of cultural sensitivity applied to human interfaces
- d6_m06 Safety Integration: Level of safety integrated into the human interface with responsible interaction safeguards

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 7: Strategy Alignment (strategy_alignment)

Describes the overall gains of coordination for AI integration strategies across distributed entities including stakeholders and domains.

Mapped Factors: standards

Metrics:
- d7_m01 Coordination Level: Level of coordination between service providers: communication channels, vertical coordination, coverage
- d7_m02 Time to Go-Live: Time delay in solution delivery from design to deployment
- d7_m03 Intent Representations: Top-level intent/vision representations and breakdown into task-specific representations
- d7_m04 Interoperability Standards: Standards on interoperability of AI systems in public administrations and private sector
- d7_m05 Service Provider Mapping: Availability of service providers and capabilities mapped to top-level intent
- d7_m06 Domain Impact: Domains impacted by the top-level intent/vision
- d7_m07 Co-benefits Analysis: Correlation and co-benefits between higher-level intents and sub-tasks
- d7_m08 International Cooperation: Metrics related to international liaisons and agreements on AI solutions

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 8: Collaboration with AI (collaboration)

Measures the level of collaboration between humans and AI in various workflows, including dynamic interaction and shaping of AI output.

Mapped Factors: opensource, standards

Metrics:
- d8_m01 Co-creation Ease: Ease of collaboration and co-creation (human in inference process)
- d8_m02 Traditional Knowledge Integration: Ability to integrate traditional knowledge into AI-based solutions
- d8_m03 Exchange Value: Value added by the exchange between humans and AI
- d8_m04 Prompting Efficiency: Prompting effort vs. quality of AI-generated component
- d8_m05 Baseline Comparison: Comparison of AI co-created output with baseline (AI-only or human-only)
- d8_m06 IAPs Supported: Incident Action Plans produced with AI techniques inputs
- d8_m07 Fine-tuning Effort: Fine-tuning and optimization efforts vs. results for open-source vs closed models

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 9: Impacts of Humans in AI Integration (human_impact)

Measures the impact of humans (AI experts, domain experts, general users) on AI integration through modeling, training, fine-tuning, and adoption.

Mapped Factors: sandbox

Metrics:
- d9_m01 Skill Distribution: Skill distribution and levels in AI, Cloud, IoT, 5G technologies
- d9_m02 Expert Intersection: Intersection of domain experts aware of AI and AI practitioners aware of domain techniques
- d9_m03 Ecosystem Readiness: Ecosystem readiness/ability to develop AI skills and talents
- d9_m04 AI Awareness: AI awareness and adoption levels among end-users
- d9_m05 Training Programs: Number of academic programmes or certified training courses in AI
- d9_m06 Experts Trained: Number of experts trained per year on AI-supported workflows
- d9_m07 Skills Gap: Skills gap analysis identifying currently lacking skills
- d9_m08 Action Latency: Inference-to-action latency: time from detection to human action

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 10: AI & Policies (ai_policies)

Two-fold: measures ability to use AI for policy experimentation and extrapolation, and readiness of policies to enable smooth AI integration.

Mapped Factors: sandbox, deployment

Metrics:
- d10_m01 Policy Sandbox: Availability of sandboxes evaluating domain-specific policies for vertical applications
- d10_m02 Policy Evaluation: Domain-specific policies and evaluation mechanisms for AI-integrated solutions
- d10_m03 Policy Extrapolation: Extrapolation mechanisms for policy interventions with simulated timeline
- d10_m04 Horizontal Policies: Availability of horizontal generic policies (data sources, AI lifecycle, explainability)
- d10_m05 Community Benefit: Number of instances where AI enables community benefit with citizen inputs
- d10_m06 Safety Policies: Policies for safe, responsible, reliable operation of AI
- d10_m07 Explainability Metrics: Metrics to measure explainability and transparency for accountability
- d10_m08 Policy Case Briefs: Number of published briefs/case studies turning operational lessons into governance lessons
- d10_m09 Audit Metrics: Metrics from audits of models, datasets, toolsets for bias, safety, explainability
- d10_m10 Data Sovereignty: Policies related to ownership and movement of data

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 11: AI for Inclusion (ai_inclusion)

Studies bridging divides in society using AI including accessibility, gender divide, and other forms of inclusion across simulation, edge AI, and GenAI.

Mapped Factors: sandbox

Metrics:
- d11_m01 Digital Twins: Number of sandbox environments and capability of simulators
- d11_m02 Sensor Types: Types of sensors (laser, cameras, gyroscope, obstacle avoidance)
- d11_m03 Edge AI Agents: Use of agents for user interface, e.g., question answers for navigation
- d11_m04 Edge Hardware: Hardware availability and affordability at the edge (CPU, GPU, memory, network)
- d11_m05 5G Connectivity: 5G connectivity for edge-to-cloud including coverage
- d11_m06 Edge Privacy: Standalone edge vs. cloud data transfer privacy
- d11_m07 Language Repository: Local grammar, dialects, and context for interaction included in language repository
- d11_m08 Regional Language Support: Offline/local-language access including offline alert kits
- d11_m09 GenAI Customization: Customizations in presentations (avatar appearances)
- d11_m10 Multi-modal Data: Different types of data processed (audio, video, images) using standard representations
- d11_m11 Beneficiaries: Number of users/beneficiaries including sign language support
- d11_m12 Women/Indigenous Leadership: Women's leadership and indigenous leadership in AI
- d11_m13 Social Inclusion Impact: Impact of AI on social inclusion decisions

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 12: Granular Priorities (granular_priorities)

Measures the availability of granular priorities in adapting AI-based solutions to subsets of users, considering local needs and context.

Mapped Factors: deployment

Metrics:
- d12_m01 Regional Priorities: Regional/domain-specific priorities and focus areas
- d12_m02 Fine-tuned Models: Fine-tuned workflows and models reflecting regional priorities
- d12_m03 Priority Organization: Existence of organizational structure for evolution of granular priorities
- d12_m04 Customized Workflows: Evolution of downstream customized workflows derived from global workflows/models

title: ITU AI Readiness Framework — 2.0 dimensions
license_note: MIT (reference repository)
text:
Dimension 13: Digital Infrastructure (digital_infrastructure)

Measures the availability of digital infrastructure including devices, computing capability, connectivity, and energy for AI deployment.

Mapped Factors: deployment

Metrics:
- d13_m01 AI-Enabled Devices: Number/quality/distribution of AI-enabled devices/sensors (ITU-T Y.3172 nodes)
- d13_m02 Data Centers: Number of data centers and APIs integrated in the overall solution
- d13_m03 Digital Services: Number of digital services integrated in cloud cross-domain solution
- d13_m04 Edge Infrastructure: Availability and utilization of edge clouds, compute at edge, connectivity to edge
- d13_m05 Energy Consumption: Energy consumption at edge, devices, and infrastructure for AI and domain-specific
- d13_m06 Energy Sustainability: Energy reliability and sustainable energy usage (power usage effectiveness)
- d13_m07 Uptime: Percentage uptime of towers/cameras and control room feeds
- d13_m08 Area Coverage: Area covered under AI services including sensors for data collection and actuators
- d13_m09 Network Quality: Quality of network connectivity (fiber, wireless, 5G coverage) per ITU-R M.2410
